newsitem.title: UK: Reckitt & Colman climbs to record high.
newsitem.headline: Reckitt & Colman climbs to record high.

text.p: Shares in household products group Reckitt and Colman Plc rose to a twelve-month intraday high on Monday, helped by a stock shortage after bid rumours resurfaced on Friday last week.

The shares rose to an all-time best of 995p to be up 30p on the day by 1305 GMT. But trading volume was a relatively slim 391,000 as market-makers said a shortage of stock had helped to squeeze the share price higher.
"There's a bit of a shortage in the market and one of the market-makers is trying to buy stock back," said one dealer.
Another trader said comments in today's Lex column of the Financial Times had also helped to lift the shares.

The newspaper pointed out that Anglo-Dutch group Unilever could probably afford to pay for Reckitt three times over by the end of this year, thanks to the sale of its speciality chemicals unit earlier this year.
On Friday, Reckitt rose 17-1/2p as rumours of a takeover bid by Unilever resurfaced following the latter's half year results.
